# Consent portal

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P3 · Act as the user](../README.md#phase-3--act-as-the-user) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:consent-portal` · **Epic:** [#156](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/156) · **Tickets:** 7 (3S 4M)

A small employee-facing UI on the CP at /portal. It lists the user's connected accounts with the agents that used each one in the last 7 days, lets the user connect or revoke a provider, and hosts the landing page for a pending authorization created by a JIT 403. Revoke deletes the stored tokens, revokes them at the provider and reaches every worker through the policy wire, so the next agent call returns authorization_required. It is off unless the CP-local consent block and --state-dir are set.

## How we build it

- Gate and mount: the portal mounts only when the CP-local `consent` block (W-P3-CSIG-01) is set and --state-dir is present. Otherwise /portal/* returns 404 and /policy stays byte-identical. The package internal/portal (created by W-P3-CSIG-02) gains an embedded index.html plus app.js (go:embed, same pattern as internal/dashboard/dashboard.go), the JSON API under /portal/api/*, and the server-rendered landing page /portal/connect/{pending_id}.
- Naming: employees see 'connections', so the API is /portal/api/connections. The word 'grants' is left to the P4 delegation grants (/portal/grants/{id}). The OAuth metadata table owned by W-P3-BRKR-02 is oauth_grants; this feature only calls the GrantStore Go API.
- Auth and isolation: every /portal route uses the W-P3-CSIG-04 portal session (__Host-warden_portal) with consent.session.idle and consent.session.absolute (the console's key names; defaults 30m and 8h from W-P3-CSIG-01). Non-GET requests require the X-Warden-CSRF header plus an Origin check; the page sends it through one shared api() wrapper (W-P1-SSO-04 convention). /portal/api/me and POST /portal/logout come from W-P3-CSIG-04 and are not added again. Console sessions, WARDEN_CP_TOKEN, worker credentials, Warden user tokens and wak_ API keys get 401, so an agent holding a delegated token can never connect, continue, decline or revoke. A sub or email on the W-P1-BLOCK-03 block list gets 403 user_blocked from the W-P3-CSIG-04 middleware (in-memory snapshot, not a per-request query), which also deletes its portal sessions; this feature adds no second check.
- Security headers on every /portal and /connect response: CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'`, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy no-referrer (the pending id never leaks to a provider), X-Content-Type-Options nosniff and Cache-Control no-store. All dynamic text is set with textContent. The page has a viewport meta tag and no fixed width over 360px.
- GET /portal/api/connections -> 200 {usage_available, usage_window_start, connections:[{provider, display_name, account_label, scopes, granted_at, last_used_at, recent_agents:[{agent, agent_display, verified, last_used_at, calls_7d}]}], available:[{provider, display_name, scopes_cap}]}. Connections come from GrantStore.ListGrants(userKey) without revoked rows, with userKey = secrets.UserKey(iss, sub) from the session; account_label is the grant's provider_account_login (W-P3-BRKR-08) and last_used_at is oauth_grants.last_used_at. `available` lists registry providers that at least one perUserSecrets wire mapping (W-P3-PUS-02) references and the user has not connected. The sub always comes from the session, never from a request parameter.
- Usage data: analytics.Event.UserTokenProvider (column user_token_provider, W-P3-PUS-10, set by W-P3-PUS-04 only when a per-user token was swapped) is separate from Event.Provider, the LLM cost provider. The fleet agent_id column is filled at ingest by W-P3-PUL-07 and user_sub comes from W-P1-VRFY-06, so this feature adds no event columns. The portal reads per-agent usage through a new typed method FleetSQLiteStore.GrantUsage(ctx, sub, since, perProviderLimit) with bind parameters, never through the Query Builder's AnalyticsQuery.Query. A connection's last_used_at is oauth_grants.last_used_at, fed by the CP mint endpoint (W-P3-PUS-07 calls GrantStore.TouchLastUsed), so it does not depend on analytics. With the memory fleet store, a query error or a 2s timeout, usage_available is false and connections still list.
- Connect and continue: the portal calls Broker.Start from W-P3-BRKR-03 and gets back the provider URL; it never sends the browser to a provider from a plain GET link an agent could post. POST /portal/api/connect {provider} -> 200 {redirect_url}; with no pending, the scope cap is provider.allowedScopes ∩ the union of scopes over every perUserSecrets mapping for that provider (passed to Broker.Start as the caller ceiling). POST /portal/api/pending/{id}/continue -> 200 {redirect_url}. POST /portal/api/pending/{id}/decline -> 200 and calls GrantStore.CompletePending(id, denied), which closes the W-P3-BRKR-02 Subscribe channel that p3-jit status waiters wait on. W-P3-BRKR-08 records the connected account (provider_account_login: the Google email or GitHub login, shown as account_label) and enforces optional consent.providers[].allowedAccountDomains.
- Pending landing: GET /portal/connect/{pending_id}. Signed-out users go to /portal/login with next set to the path; next must be a relative path under /portal/ or /connect/ with no scheme, no `//` and no backslash (the W-P3-CSIG-02 rule). The page shows only text Warden builds: the agent display name with a verified or unregistered badge from the agent registry (W-P2-AREG-04 wire), the provider, the capped scopes, the request host, method and MCP tool when the pending carries them (W-P3-BRKR-02 request columns, filled by W-P3-JIT-01), the expiry as a relative time from the CP clock, and 'Signed in as <email>. Not you? Sign out'. There is no free-text agent message. Unknown, expired, terminal and other users' pending ids all return 404 with the same body.
- Revoke: POST /portal/api/connections/{provider}/revoke -> 200 {status: revoked|partial, steps:{grant, secret_delete, epoch, provider_revoke: ok|pending|failed|skipped}, workers_without_cap}, 404 when no grant was ever recorded, 409 while a revoke for the same (user, provider) is running, and an idempotent 200 for an already revoked grant. It calls the shared oauthbroker.RevokeUserGrant(ctx, iss, sub, provider, Actor{ID, Kind: user|admin|system, Reason}), which W-P3-OFFB-01 reuses with Kind system. Steps run inside Engine.WithGrantLock(userKey, provider) (W-P3-PUS-03, over the oauthbroker.GrantLocks mutex shared with the BRKR-04 callback), which also drops the CP token cache entry: (1) read the TokenRecord into memory; (2) GrantStore.RevokeGrant; (3) delete users/<userKey>/<provider> from consent.store; (4) EpochStore.Bump(userKey) (W-P3-PUS-08, through the W-P3-PORT-05 adapter) so workers drop cached tokens; (5) oauthbroker.Revoke (W-P3-BRKR-05) with the in-memory token. Delete runs before the bump, so a mint after eviction finds nothing.
- Worker invalidation: the userGrantEpochs signed-bundle section from W-P3-PUS-08 ({userKey: epoch}, epoch = the publish_log seq of the bump, pruned after 2 x workerCacheTTL) is the only revocation channel to workers; this feature adds no table, wire field or heartbeat cap of its own. The section lives outside policy versions, so a rollback never un-revokes, and its keys are user keys, so no sub appears on the wire.
- Worker side: W-P3-PUS-09 evicts cached tokens on each verified bundle apply and caps any cached token at perUserSecrets.workerCacheTTL (at most 15m), which also bounds GitHub tokens that never expire. Workers never write tokens back; only the CP refresh engine does, and it re-checks grant state, epoch and grant_id first (W-P3-PUS-03, W-P3-PUS-06). Workers that enforce this advertise heartbeat cap usersecrets/v1, and the revoke response lists connected workers without it (W-P3-PORT-05).
- Failure handling: if the provider revoke fails with a retryable error, the TokenRecord is parked in consent.store at secrets.RevokingKey(userKey, provider) = revoking/<userKey>/<provider> and a CP ticker retries with backoff for up to 24h, then deletes it and raises an alert through internal/alertpipeline. A non-retryable failure gives up at once and the UI shows the provider's manual revoke link. An orphan sweep, run about 2 minutes after each revoke and on every CP retention tick, lists users/ metadata in consent.store (never values) and deletes any users/<userKey>/<provider> key that has no active oauth_grants row; this removes a rotated refresh token that a racing CP refresh wrote back after the delete.
- Audit and logs: when console.adminAudit.enabled, connect.started, connect.declined and connect.revoked are recorded through adminaudit.Recorder (W-P1-AAUD-01) with new auth_method portal, target_ref grant:<provider> and per-step outcomes in details, never a token or secret Reference value. A structured log line with the same fields is always written, and W-P1-JAUD-03 emits the warden.admin.v1 line when admin audit is on. Unauthenticated requests are never chained. Logs never contain tokens, codes, cookies or CSRF tokens.
- Degraded modes: CP down means the portal is unavailable and workers serve cached tokens for at most workerCacheTTL. IdP down means existing sessions keep working and /portal/login returns 503 idp_unavailable. Provider down means connect shows an error page and revoke takes the retry path. A CP restart loses nothing, because sessions, pendings, epochs and the retry queue are in cpstate. Mutating portal endpoints are limited to 10 per minute per session. GrantStore and the epoch store are interfaces, so p5-postgres-ha can replace them.

## Done when

On a CP with the consent block, --state-dir and a Vault or AWS consent.store, an employee signed in at /portal sees each connected provider with its account label, scopes, last_used_at and only the agents that used their own grant in the last 7 days. They can connect a new provider within the computed scope cap, and open a pending link an agent posted to either continue (the pending becomes granted) or decline (it becomes denied); another user's or an expired pending id shows the same 404 page. Revoking a provider leaves no users/<userKey>/<provider> key in consent.store even after a simulated racing refresh write-back, the fake provider receives a revoke call, a failed provider revoke shows as pending and is retried, and within one long-poll cycle the next agent call through that mapping returns authorization_required on every usersecrets/v1 worker, including one holding a cached token. Bearer tokens and API keys get 401 on every portal route, the pages refuse to load in a frame, and with the consent block absent /portal returns 404 and /policy bytes are unchanged.

### 1/7 · W-P3-PORT-01

**Serve the portal page and the connections list API**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#157](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/157)

Add the embedded portal page and GET /portal/api/connections so an employee can see which providers they connected and which agents used each one in the last 7 days. Usage comes from a new typed, bind-parameter query on the fleet store keyed on the user_token_provider column (W-P3-PUS-10), because Event.Provider already means the LLM cost provider. The ticket also adds the shared portal security headers that every later portal route reuses. It is CP-only and mounted only when the consent block is set.

**Requirements**

- Routes: GET /portal (embedded index.html and app.js) and GET /portal/api/connections, mounted on the CP mux in controlplane.Server.Handler only when the consent block and --state-dir are set; otherwise both return 404 and /policy body and ETag are unchanged. /portal/api/me and /portal/logout are reused from W-P3-CSIG-04, not added again.
- Response: 200 {usage_available, usage_window_start, connections:[{provider, display_name, account_label, scopes, granted_at, last_used_at, recent_agents:[{agent, agent_display, verified, last_used_at, calls_7d}]}], available:[{provider, display_name, scopes_cap}]}. Connections come from GrantStore.ListGrants(secrets.UserKey(iss, sub)) without revoked rows, with account_label = provider_account_login (W-P3-BRKR-08); `available` lists registry providers referenced by at least one perUserSecrets wire mapping and not yet connected, with scopes_cap = allowedScopes ∩ the union of that provider's mapping scopes.
- Usage: new analytics.GrantUsageReader interface with GrantUsage(ctx, sub string, since time.Time, perProviderLimit int) ([]GrantUsage, error), implemented by FleetSQLiteStore with fixed SQL and bind parameters, grouping by user_token_provider and agent_id over the columns from W-P3-PUS-10, W-P3-PUL-07 and W-P1-VRFY-06, with a new index (user_sub, user_token_provider, ts). The query never goes through AnalyticsQuery.Query.
- A connection's last_used_at is oauth_grants.last_used_at (fed by W-P3-PUS-07 mints); recent_agents[].last_used_at is MAX(ts) from GrantUsage. With the memory fleet store, a query error or the 2s query timeout, the endpoint still returns 200 with recent_agents [] and usage_available false. usage_window_start reports the oldest event the store still holds inside the 7-day window.
- Isolation: the sub is taken only from the portal session Principal. Requests with no portal session, a console session, a bearer token or a wak_ API key get 401. A blocked principal gets 403 {"error":"user_blocked"} from the W-P3-CSIG-04 middleware.
- Headers on every /portal and /connect response: CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'`, X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, Cache-Control no-store. The page sends X-Warden-CSRF through one api() wrapper and sets all dynamic text with textContent.
- Performance and logs: p95 for /portal/api/connections under 150 ms with 1M fleet events in the window. One debug log line `msg=portal_connections provider_count usage_available duration_ms`; no tokens, secret References, cookies or email in logs.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/analytics/fleet.go: add the new GrantUsageReader interface and GrantUsage result type {Provider, Agent, LastUsedAt, Calls7d}.
2. internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go: in FleetSQLiteStore.migrate add the (user_sub, user_token_provider, ts) index idempotently; implement GrantUsage with one parameterized GROUP BY user_token_provider, agent_id query under a 2s context timeout.
3. internal/portal/headers.go (new): securityHeaders middleware.
4. internal/portal/connections.go (new): handler for GET /portal/api/connections that combines GrantStore.ListGrants, the perUserSecrets wire snapshot, the oauthbroker provider registry and GrantUsage (type-asserted from the CP central store), and resolves agent display names from the agent registry wire (W-P2-AREG-04).
5. internal/portal/portal.go: add `//go:embed index.html app.js`, serve GET /portal, and wrap all routes in the CSIG-04 session middleware and securityHeaders.
6. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go Handler(): mount /portal and /portal/ next to the CSIG routes only when the consent block is configured.
7. Tests: internal/portal/connections_test.go (users A and B with seeded grants and events, sub with SQL metacharacters, console cookie and bearer get 401, blocked sub gets 403, revoked grant hidden, memory store gives usage_available false); internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite_test.go TestGrantUsage (migration idempotent on an old DB); internal/controlplane TestPortalNotMountedWithoutConsent; a header test and a check that index.html has a viewport meta tag.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given user A with an active Google grant seeded through GrantStore.BeginGrant and ActivateGrant and fleet events with user_token_provider=google, When A calls GET /portal/api/connections with a portal session, Then the response is 200 with provider google, its scopes, account_label, granted_at and last_used_at equal to the grant's last_used_at.
- [ ] Given google events from agents X and Y for user A and agent Z for user B, When A lists connections, Then recent_agents holds exactly X and Y with correct calls_7d and Z never appears. Verified by `go test ./internal/portal -run TestConnectionsScopedToSub` and `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestGrantUsage`.
- [ ] Given a CP using the memory fleet store, When connections are listed, Then the response is 200 with recent_agents [] and usage_available false.
- [ ] Given a CP config with no consent block, When GET /portal or /portal/api/connections is requested, Then the response is 404 and the /policy body and ETag are byte-identical. Verified by `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestPortalNotMountedWithoutConsent`.
- [ ] Given no portal session, a console session cookie, a bearer token or a wak_ key, Then /portal/api/connections returns 401; given a blocked sub, it returns 403 user_blocked; and every /portal response carries frame-ancestors 'none', Referrer-Policy no-referrer and Cache-Control no-store.

### 2/7 · W-P3-PORT-02

**Implement revoke with grant, secret, epoch and provider steps**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#158](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/158)

Add POST /portal/api/connections/{provider}/revoke and the shared oauthbroker.RevokeUserGrant that offboarding also calls. It marks the grant revoked, deletes the live secret, bumps the user's grant epoch so workers drop cached tokens, and revokes the token at the provider, reporting each step. The order matters: the secret is deleted before the epoch bump so a worker that re-reads after eviction finds nothing. This ticket is CP-only; worker application is W-P3-PORT-06 and the provider retry queue is W-P3-PORT-07.

**Requirements**

- New `oauthbroker.RevokeUserGrant(ctx, iss, sub, provider string, by Actor) (RevokeResult, error)` with Actor{ID, Kind: user|admin|system, Reason}; userKey = secrets.UserKey(iss, sub). EpochBumper (`Bump(ctx, userKey) error`, the W-P3-PUS-08 EpochStore through the W-P3-PORT-05 adapter) and adminaudit.Recorder are injected through the Broker constructor, so oauthbroker never imports controlplane.
- Step order, each attempted after earlier failures: read the TokenRecord into memory; GrantStore.RevokeGrant; delete secrets.UserGrantKey(userKey, provider) from consent.store; EpochBumper.Bump; oauthbroker.Revoke (W-P3-BRKR-05). A missing token skips provider_revoke and still runs the others. Steps run inside Engine.WithGrantLock (W-P3-PUS-03), which takes the oauthbroker.GrantLocks mutex shared with the W-P3-BRKR-04 callback and drops the CP token cache entry.
- Responses: 200 {status: revoked|partial, steps:{grant, secret_delete, epoch, provider_revoke: ok|pending|failed|skipped}, workers_without_cap:[...]} when secret_delete succeeds; 502 when secret_delete fails; 404 for an unknown provider or no recorded grant; 409 while a revoke for the same key is running; 200 with the same terminal state for an already revoked grant; 403 without a valid X-Warden-CSRF; 401 without a portal session.
- workers_without_cap lists connected workers whose heartbeat lacks usersecrets/v1 (W-P3-PORT-05), so the user and operator know propagation is not guaranteed there.
- Audit: when admin audit is enabled, exactly one connect.revoked row through adminaudit.Recorder with new auth_method portal (offboarding passes Kind system), target_ref grant:<provider> and per-step outcomes in details. A `msg=connect_revoked provider outcome steps duration_ms` log line is always written. Tokens, secret Reference values and provider error bodies are never logged or returned.
- Limits: the provider call is capped at 5s and the whole revoke at 10s; mutating portal routes are limited to 10 per minute per session.
- index.html/app.js: a Revoke button with a confirm dialog, a partial-result banner and the provider's manual revoke link for a non-retryable failure.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/oauthbroker/revoke_user.go (new): Actor, RevokeResult, the EpochBumper interface and RevokeUserGrant with the step order above.
2. Run the steps inside Engine.WithGrantLock (W-P3-PUS-03) over the W-P3-BRKR-04 GrantLocks; add no second lock.
3. internal/portal/revoke.go (new): POST /portal/api/connections/{provider}/revoke behind CSIG-04 CSRF, provider checked against the registry, sub from the session only, 409 on lock contention, plus the rate limiter shared by mutating portal routes.
4. internal/controlplane: read heartbeat caps from the worker registry to fill workers_without_cap.
5. Record connect.revoked through adminaudit.Recorder when enabled and always write the structured log line.
6. internal/portal/app.js: Revoke button, confirm dialog and result banner.
7. Tests: internal/oauthbroker/revoke_user_test.go (fake provider sees the revoke, users/<userKey>/google absent from fakes.MemorySecretStore, provider 503 still deletes and returns partial, second call is idempotent, -race test with a concurrent callback write); internal/portal/revoke_test.go (CSRF 403, unknown provider 404, audit row written, log capture holds no token).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given user A with a Google grant written by the fake provider flow, When A POSTs /portal/api/connections/google/revoke with a valid X-Warden-CSRF, Then the response is 200 status revoked, fakes.MemorySecretStore has no users/<userKey>/google key, the fake revoke endpoint received the refresh token, revoked_at is set and A's epoch increased. Verified by `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRevokeUserGrant`.
- [ ] Given the fake provider revoke endpoint returns 503, When A revokes, Then the live key is still deleted, the grant is revoked, the epoch is bumped and the response is 200 status partial with provider_revoke pending.
- [ ] Given a callback write for (A, google) racing a revoke, When both run under `go test -race ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRevokeCallbackRace`, Then the live key is absent after both finish.
- [ ] Given a POST without X-Warden-CSRF, or a revoke for a provider A never connected, Then the responses are 403 and 404 and no store, provider or epoch call is made. Verified by `go test ./internal/portal -run TestRevoke`.
- [ ] Given admin audit is enabled, When A revokes, Then exactly one admin_audit row with action connect.revoked and auth_method portal is written, and no log line or row contains the access or refresh token.

### 3/7 · W-P3-PORT-03

**Add the pending landing page and connect, continue and decline actions**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#159](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/159)

Add GET /portal/connect/{pending_id}, the page an agent's authorize_url points to, plus the POST actions that start a connection or decline it. The page shows only text Warden builds from the pending row and the agent registry, never text the agent supplied, so it cannot be used for consent phishing. Continue and connect are CSRF-protected POSTs that return the provider URL, so a link an agent posts can never send the browser straight to a provider consent screen. CP-only.

**Requirements**

- GET /portal/connect/{pending_id} requires a portal session; with none it redirects to /portal/login?next=/portal/connect/<id>. next must be a relative path under /portal/ or /connect/ with no scheme, `//` or backslash; anything else falls back to /portal (the W-P3-CSIG-02 rule).
- Content: agent display name with a verified or unregistered badge from the agent registry wire, provider display name, capped scopes with descriptions, the request host, method and MCP tool from the W-P3-BRKR-02 request columns when set (W-P3-JIT-01 fills them), the expiry as a relative time computed from the CP clock, and 'Signed in as <email>. Not you? Sign out'. No free text from the agent is ever rendered; every value is set with textContent.
- Unknown, expired, terminal and other users' pending ids return 404 with a byte-identical generic body that holds no agent, provider or scope string.
- Actions, all with X-Warden-CSRF, an Origin check and the portal session only: POST /portal/api/pending/{id}/continue -> 200 {redirect_url}; POST /portal/api/pending/{id}/decline -> 200, calling GrantStore.CompletePending(id, denied), which closes the W-P3-BRKR-02 Subscribe channel that p3-jit status waiters use; POST /portal/api/connect {provider} -> 200 {redirect_url} with scope cap allowedScopes ∩ the union of that provider's perUserSecrets scopes. Terminal pending -> 409 only for its owner.
- The redirect URL comes from Broker.Start (W-P3-BRKR-03); POST /portal/api/connect passes the allowedScopes ∩ perUserSecrets ceiling, and GET /connect/start only redirects to the portal (W-P3-BRKR-03), so a posted link never lands on a provider consent screen.
- Audit: connect.started and connect.declined through adminaudit.Recorder with auth_method portal when enabled; log `msg=portal_pending_view outcome=shown|not_available|declined provider` with only the first 8 characters of the pending id.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/portal/connect.go (new): GET /portal/connect/{id} with GrantStore.GetPending, owner and status checks, and html/template rendering of embedded connect.html; one notAvailable() writer for every 404 case.
2. internal/portal/connect.go: POST /portal/api/pending/{id}/continue and POST /portal/api/connect calling the BRKR-03 start function, and POST /portal/api/pending/{id}/decline calling CompletePending(id, denied).
3. internal/portal/connect.html and app.js (new): the landing layout, the Continue and Decline buttons that post through api() and then set window.location to redirect_url, and the Connect buttons on the connections page.
4. Validate next through a shared safeNext(path) helper and use it in the signed-out redirect.
5. Record connect.started and connect.declined audit rows and the log line.
6. Tests in internal/portal/connect_test.go: signed-out redirect and return after the fake login; open-redirect next rejected; foreign, expired and random ids give identical 404 bodies; decline closes the pending's Subscribe channel; decline and continue without CSRF return 403; continue returns a provider URL whose scopes are capped.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a signed-out browser, When it opens /portal/connect/<id>, Then it is redirected to /portal/login with next=/portal/connect/<id> and lands back on that page after the fake OIDC login; a next of `//evil.example` or `https://evil.example` falls back to /portal. Verified by `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPendingLandingLoginRedirect`.
- [ ] Given user A's active pending for registered agent X, provider google and scopes [gmail.readonly], When A opens the page, Then it shows X with a verified badge, Google, gmail.readonly and the relative expiry, and no field from the request other than these.
- [ ] Given A's pending and a GrantStore Subscribe channel for it, When A POSTs decline with a valid X-Warden-CSRF, Then the pending is denied and the channel closes within 1s. Verified by `go test ./internal/portal -run TestPendingDecline`.
- [ ] Given user B's pending id, an expired pending and a random id, When A opens each page, Then all three return 404 with byte-identical bodies.
- [ ] Given POST /portal/api/connect {provider: google} with a valid CSRF token, Then the redirect_url requests only allowedScopes ∩ the union of google perUserSecrets scopes; and continue or decline without X-Warden-CSRF returns 403 with the pending unchanged.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-PORT-01`](consent-portal.md#17--w-p3-port-01) Serve the portal page and the connections list API; [`W-P3-CSIG-02`](consent-auth.md#27--w-p3-csig-02) Implement portal login, callback and session store; [`W-P3-BRKR-03`](oauth-broker.md#39--w-p3-brkr-03) Implement POST /connect/start with PKCE, CSRF and scope capping

### 4/7 · W-P3-PORT-04

**Write the consent portal user and operator guide**

Type **docs** · Size **S** · Issue [#160](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/160)

Add docs/consent-portal.md so operators can register provider apps, configure the consent block and set least-privilege secret backend access, and so employees know what the portal shows. It documents how revoke propagates to workers, its time bound, and what a partial revoke means. The config example is parsed by a test so it cannot drift.

**Requirements**

- Provider registration for Google and GitHub (redirect URI <cp>/connect/callback, scopes per perUserSecrets, Google access_type=offline and prompt=consent) and the Dex `warden-portal` static client with redirect /portal/callback (W-P3-CSIG-01 carry-forward).
- Config reference with the aligned keys: consent.oidc.*, consent.session.idle, consent.session.absolute, consent.providers[] including allowedAccountDomains, consent.store, perUserSecrets.workerCacheTTL and the defaults. State that the portal is off when the block is absent and that the CP origin must be reachable by employees' browsers but never needs to be on an agent allowlist.
- Least-privilege IAM and Vault policies: the CP role gets create, read, update, delete and list on the consent.store prefix (default warden-cp/*); worker roles and the secretStore credential the CP distributes to workers get no access to it (W-P3-CSIG-06). Include the commands for loading `oauth-clients/<id>` client secrets directly in the backend (W-P3-BRKR-06). Update the comment in internal/secrets/store.go that says workers only Get.
- Data map: what cpstate holds (portal_sessions, grant metadata, pending_authorizations, user_grant_epochs, the revoke retry queue) and what stays only in consent.store (users/, idp/, revoking/ and oauth-clients/ keys holding access, refresh and Dex refresh tokens and client secrets), plus the fleet event columns user_sub, agent_id and user_token_provider.
- Revoke propagation: step order, partial results, the epoch on the wire, the bound (one long-poll cycle for usersecrets/v1 workers; at most workerCacheTTL when the CP is unreachable), the retry window, the orphan sweep and the providers' manual revoke links. Also the security headers and the X-Warden-CSRF header.
- The doc holds no real client secrets; examples use env var names.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write docs/consent-portal.md with sections for provider registration, Dex client, config, IAM, data map, employee view and revoke propagation.
2. Add one fenced `yaml consent-example` block with a complete consent config.
3. Add internal/config/consent_doc_test.go TestConsentPortalDocExample, which extracts that block and loads it through the strict config parser.
4. Update the internal/secrets/store.go doc comment about worker access.
5. Link the doc from docs/control-plane.md and run `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go check` and `scripts/check.sh`.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given docs/consent-portal.md, When `go test ./internal/config -run TestConsentPortalDocExample` runs, Then the yaml consent-example block parses and validates with no errors.
- [ ] The IAM section grants workers no access to the consent.store prefix.
- [ ] The doc uses consent.session.idle, consent.session.absolute and X-Warden-CSRF consistently with docs/control-plane.md, and `scripts/check.sh` passes.
- [ ] The doc states the revoke propagation bound and lists every cpstate table and secret path it mentions.

### 5/7 · W-P3-PORT-05

**Bump grant epochs on revoke and report workers without usersecrets/v1**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#295](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/295)

Revoke reaches workers through the userGrantEpochs signed-bundle section that W-P3-PUS-08 owns, not through a second channel. Add the CP adapter that lets oauthbroker.RevokeUserGrant bump a user's epoch without importing controlplane, and report which connected workers could still serve a cached token because they lack heartbeat cap usersecrets/v1. CP-only; without the consent block nothing is created and /policy is unchanged.

**Requirements**

- internal/controlplane implements oauthbroker.EpochBumper{Bump(ctx, userKey) error} over EpochStore.Bump (W-P3-PUS-08) and passes it to the Broker constructor; oauthbroker never imports controlplane.
- A failed Bump is returned to RevokeUserGrant, which reports epoch: failed and status partial; the secret is already deleted, so a later mint still finds nothing.
- New WorkerCapsReader{WorkersWithoutCap(cap string) []string} over the heartbeat caps the worker registry already stores (W-P1-BLOCK-10); RevokeUserGrant returns workers_without_cap for usersecrets/v1.
- No second epoch table, wire field, retention key or heartbeat cap is added; keys are secrets.UserKey values from W-P3-CSIG-06.
- Logs `msg=grant_epoch_bumped key_prefix` with the first 8 characters of the user key, never the sub.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/controlplane/grantepochs_adapter.go (new): the EpochBumper and WorkerCapsReader adapters.
2. Wire both into the Broker in controlplane.Server construction when the consent block is set.
3. Tests in internal/controlplane/grantepochs_adapter_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a bundle long-poll, When RevokeUserGrant bumps user A through the adapter, Then the poll returns within 1s with sections.userGrantEpochs[userKey(A)] higher than before and no sub in the body. Verified by `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestGrantEpochAdapter`.
- [ ] Given two connected workers of which one advertises usersecrets/v1, Then workers_without_cap lists only the other.
- [ ] Given a failing EpochStore, Then RevokeUserGrant returns status partial with epoch failed and the secret already deleted.
- [ ] Given no consent block, Then the /policy body and ETag are unchanged.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-PUS-08`](refresh-model.md#812--w-p3-pus-08) Serve perUserSecrets and userGrantEpochs as signed-bundle sections; [`W-P3-BRKR-02`](oauth-broker.md#29--w-p3-brkr-02) Add pending authorization, attempt and grant metadata stores; [`W-P1-BLOCK-10`](user-block-list.md#1012--w-p1-block-10) Advertise and record worker caps (blocklist/v1) in the heartbeat

### 6/7 · W-P3-PORT-06

**Prove portal revoke end to end on usersecrets/v1 workers**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#296](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/296)

Own the integration test for the feature's revoke promise: after a user revokes a provider in the portal, the next agent call through that mapping returns authorization_required on every usersecrets/v1 worker, including one that holds a cached token. Worker eviction is W-P3-PUS-09 and the 403 comes from W-P3-PUS-04 (later the W-P3-JIT-02 body), so this ticket changes no production code beyond test fakes.

**Requirements**

- New test/integration/portal_revoke_test.go (build tag integration): a CP with consent, the broker, perUserSecrets and signed bundles; one enrolled worker with a cert bound to a registered agent; the fake OAuth provider and a fake upstream that records Authorization.
- Flow: connect Google through the portal, an agent call succeeds and caches the token, revoke through POST /portal/api/connections/google/revoke, then the next call returns 403 authorization_required within one long-poll cycle with zero upstream requests carrying the old token.
- A fake heartbeat for a worker without usersecrets/v1 makes that worker appear in workers_without_cap.
- Captured logs, events and metrics contain no access or refresh token.

**Implementation plan**

1. test/integration/portal_revoke_test.go reusing the stack helpers from the W-P3-BRKR-09 and W-P3-PUS-11 tests.
2. A fake heartbeat client for the old-worker case.
3. A token byte search over captured logs, events and metrics at the end.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -tags integration ./test/integration -run TestPortalRevokeE2E` passes.
- [ ] The first agent call reaches the upstream with A's token, and the post-revoke call returns 403 authorization_required within 5s with zero upstream requests using the revoked token.
- [ ] The revoke response lists the fake old worker in workers_without_cap, and the token byte search finds nothing.

### 7/7 · W-P3-PORT-07

**Add provider revoke retries and the orphan token sweep**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#297](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/297)

Make a revoke finish even when the provider is down or a racing CP refresh writes a rotated token back after the delete. A retryable provider failure parks the token under the reserved revoking/ prefix of consent.store and a CP ticker retries it for up to 24h before alerting. An orphan sweep deletes any live per-user key that has no active grant row, using metadata-only List. CP-only.

**Requirements**

- On a retryable error from oauthbroker.Revoke, RevokeUserGrant parks the TokenRecord in consent.store at secrets.RevokingKey(userKey, provider) and inserts a cpstate revoke_retries(user_key, provider, attempts, next_at, first_failed_at) row; provider_revoke reports pending. A non-retryable error gives up at once and reports failed with the provider's manual revoke URL.
- A CP ticker retries due rows with exponential backoff (1m doubling, max 1h) for up to 24h, then deletes the parked key, marks the row given up and raises an alert through internal/alertpipeline. A success deletes the parked key and the row.
- Orphan sweep about 2 minutes after each revoke and on every CP retention tick: consent.store List over users/ (metadata only, never values) and Delete on any users/<userKey>/<provider> key with no active oauth_grants row; idp/ and revoking/ keys are outside the listed prefix.
- Each sweep deletion logs `msg=portal_revoke_resurrected provider key_prefix` and increments a CP counter; values are never read or logged.
- Restart safe: the retry queue lives in cpstate and resumes after a CP restart. Without the consent block nothing runs.
- Revoke results report pending until the retry succeeds; GET /portal/api/connections shows the connection as revoking while a retry row exists.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/oauthbroker/revoke_retry.go (new): revoke_retries migration, park(userKey, provider, rec), retry loop with backoff and the 24h give-up.
2. Hook park into RevokeUserGrant on a retryable BRKR-05 error.
3. internal/oauthbroker/sweep.go (new): orphan sweep over SecretStore.List and GrantStore.ListGrants.
4. internal/controlplane: start the retry ticker and call the sweep from the retention ticker and after each revoke.
5. Raise the give-up alert through internal/alertpipeline.
6. Tests: internal/oauthbroker/revoke_retry_test.go (503 then 200 deletes the parked key; 24h give-up deletes and alerts using a fake clock; queue resumes after store reopen) and sweep_test.go (a Put after delete is removed; idp/ and revoking/ keys untouched).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given the fake provider returns 503 on the first revoke and 200 later, When the retry ticker runs, Then the parked revoking/ key is deleted, the row is gone and the fake provider saw the token. Verified by `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestRevokeRetry`.
- [ ] Given the provider fails for 24h of fake-clock time, Then the parked key is deleted and one alert is raised.
- [ ] Given a Put of a rotated token to A's users/<userKey>/google key after the revoke (a racing CP refresh), When the orphan sweep runs, Then the key is deleted and one portal_revoke_resurrected line is logged. Verified by `go test ./internal/oauthbroker -run TestOrphanSweep`.
- [ ] Given idp/<userKey> and revoking/ keys, When the sweep runs, Then they are untouched and no secret value was read.

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-PORT-02`](consent-portal.md#27--w-p3-port-02) Implement revoke with grant, secret, epoch and provider steps

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-PORT-04`](consent-portal.md#47--w-p3-port-04) Write the consent portal user and operator guide; [`W-P3-OFFB-01`](offboarding.md#17--w-p3-offb-01) Implement the resumable two-stage Offboarder
